GS constructs bundles, shtukas and Langlands but not Yu's counts, recurrence and universal polynomials; the Part II is justified and its title has the parent prefix. The review added eleven missing items (Lafforgue's cutoff formula and the T-semistable indicator, periodicity of the isocline count, automorphic inertial twists, Frobenius pullback, stabiliser orders and cuspidal-pair counts, the Jacobian-factor division, Gauss's lemma, the top-weight term) and appended the corrections the layers must respect: Lemme A.2 needs gcd(e, n) = 1, so Théorème 1.4 in general must be imported from Mellit; the top-weight assertion of Théorème 1.1(1) needs a proof; g ≥ 2 in Lemme 7.3.1 and its cone argument; (5.3.2); Théorème 3.3.1 on lattice points. (First review: Part II of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands for the counting machinery, taking 67 of the 120 missing items. The title reproduces the parent's atlas title ('Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields') exactly, the area functionfields is a galaxy id, and the 226-word brief states what the new layers must build. The direction is the parent's: it constructs shtukas and the Langlands correspondence over function fields, and this paper counts the ℓ-adic local systems that correspondence classifies, through a trace formula the parent does not carry.)

This extraction is the only proposer of the roadmap, so the change desynchronises nothing.)

notes: Two independent reviews. FIRST (cc-7b31c4, #2388, structural): Accept. 154 items, 11 library, 23 planned and 120 missing, every missing item routed exactly once across thirteen routes, with 27 sourceIssues. I reproduced the recorded hash of arXiv v5 (9383bcde…), the 85-page text the extraction read. Structure: every stage named by the eleven source routes exists, all 18 distinct planned layer ids exist, and all fifteen declarations behind the eleven library items exist at the pinned commits — including the Tau Ceti ones (Divisor.finite_ker_degreeClass, isRiemannRochDivisor_weilDifferentialDivisor, repRing and repRingCharacter) and the less obvious Mathlib ones (Matrix.det_one_sub_mul_comm, ArithmeticFunction.sum_eq_iff_sum_smul_moebius_eq, UnitAddTorus.hasSum_mFourier_series_apply_of_summable, AddChar.expect_eq_ite). Both Part II routes reproduce their parent's title exactly, and the second correctly uses the Part II mechanism to extend a Tau Ceti roadmap rather than re-planning it. Its area was 'algebra', which is not a galaxy id in data/galaxies.json; I corrected it to 'representations'. This is the same corpus-wide problem I recorded in REV-PAPER-LESLIE-25, where I did not correct it because five extractions shared the roadmap and the area with it; here this extraction is the only proposer, so the change is safe and desynchronises nothing. Locators: 86 of 99 checks land on exactly the page given, and the thirteen others are artefacts of a locator format that mixes this paper's sections with other works' numbering — 'Laf97 p227' is a page of Lafforgue, 'KS99 Theorems 10.6.10–10.6.11' are Kottwitz–Shelstad's, and several pages attach to a § rather than to a numbered statement. The one genuine boundary case is Corollaire 2.3.3, which begins at the foot of p. 10 and is cited at p. 11 by three items. The 27 findings are dense and technical, fifteen of them affecting a proof. I verified the one that is settled by a one-line computation and it holds: (6.1.1) on p. 42 prints H^0_c(X, F_1 ⊗ F_2^∨) ≅ Hom_X(F_1, F_2) and (6.1.2) prints H^2_c ≅ Hom_X(F_2, F_1)^∨(−1), whereas F_1 ⊗ F_2^∨ is Hom(F_2, F_1), so the two Hom arguments are indeed reversed, exactly as E14 says. The others I read are of the same character — a sign, an index range, an ambient ring, a multiplicity — each with a specific repair and an honest reach. Nothing was rejected and no item was deleted. SECOND (cc-39fac3, holder of the claim on #1092, content): Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-39fac3, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by cc-442dc5 and Codex sessions a71f92 and c83e7a. The published version (Ann. of Math. 197 (2023), 423–531) is paywalled, so the review read arXiv v5 (the version the extraction read) and its TeX in full again with four checkers (§§1–3 and Appendix B; §§4–5; §6; §7 and Appendices A, C), who also checked numerically: the rank-two and rank-three examples of p. 5, the integrality and cone claims from Mellit's formula for small g, n, Lemma 6.3.2(b), and Lemme A.2. Statements: 30 corrected (among them 069, 084, 116, 119 and 020). Locators: 46. Statuses: 013 and 020 planned → missing. Library citations all exist at the pinned commits. The extraction's repairs and derivations (012, 032, 045, 046, 079, 083, 084, 110, 118, 129, 142–153) are sound; 116's is sound only for gcd(e, n) = 1. 25 new items (4 planned, 21 missing). E1–E27 confirmed; nine reclassified to affect nothing (E15 from gap to misprint). 29 new source issues, the substantive ones being: Lemme A.2 is false when gcd(e, n) > 1, so the paper's proof of Théorème 1.4 covers only e prime to n (the theorem itself is Mellit's in general); the top-weight assertion of Théorème 1.1(1) is never proved (it is true, and a proof is sketched); (5.3.2) pairs each root with the wrong Rankin–Selberg factor (Proposition 5.1.1 unaffected); gaps in Lemme 7.3.1's cone argument, Théorème 7.2.3 for non-positive S_i, Lemme 4.2.5's Haar normalisation and Appendix B's quasi-polynomiality; Théorème 3.3.1 only on lattice points. Théorèmes 1.1–1.3 hold as stated.
